solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In which one pursues mate without seeing any men

definitions.text: In which one pursues mate without seeing any men

parts.words: In which one pursues mate without seeing any men
parts.note: the mate is checkmate and the men are chess pieces, played from memory with the board out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a partner while never meeting a single man, like a hopeless romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' and 'men' read as romance, but they are chess terms: checkmate and the pieces. The player never looks at the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of the board game played without sight of the pieces, moves being called out and remembered.

clue.text: Source of gratuitous advice from champion behind golf club

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
a seat is the buttocks, one's behind
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A champion player standing behind a golf club offers unwanted tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word, but it is a noun meaning bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who gives the motorist unwanted instructions; by extension anyone offering unasked-for interference.

clue.text: Young female patient swallowing drug that's banned

indicators.note: swallowing means the drug letter is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: a patient is someone ill
gal is an informal word for a girl
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A young woman in hospital takes a prohibited substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illegal is forbidden by law, i.e. prohibited.

clue.text: Avoiding any misunderstanding, on way back from car trip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: making a point forcefully so it is fully understood

definitions.text: on way back from car trip
definitions.meaning: second meaning: motoring back to one's house

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'drive a point home' means to make it absolutely clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an idiom for emphatic clarity and a literal description of motoring to your house.

clue.text: Picked for team in position on pitch that's okay

definitions.meaning: first meaning: selected and so on the side

definitions.text: in position on pitch that's okay
definitions.meaning: second meaning: not offside, legally positioned in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A player selected for the squad stands in a legal spot on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: A pitch is a sports field; a player ahead of the ball in some positions is offside, the opposite being onside.
explanation.definitionFit: Onside means both belonging to the team and positioned legally under the offside law; it also means in agreement.

clue.text: Planned action without notice

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the action word goes around the notice

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a sign is a notice put up

explanation.surface: A deliberate act carried out with no warning given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designed has been devised or intended in advance, i.e. done on purpose.

clue.text: Keeps contents of the case

indicators.note: contents of takes the inner letters of the words the and case, dropping their ends

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to what is inside the suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to hold or possess it.

clue.text: Language I wish a learner could translate into

indicators.note: translate here means change form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A wish that a student could render something into another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translate' fits a language clue, but it signals rearranging WISH A into SWAHI; then come L for learner and the I from the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: In this cause, nut becomes excited? Just the opposite

definitions.note: the definition is the reverse of excited, the word before it

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of in this cause nut are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A fanatic gets worked up about a cause, or maybe not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' serves twice in spirit: it stirs the fodder, and the definition is its opposite, lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lukewarm or lacking keenness is the reverse of being thrilled.

clue.text: Scientist, remembered by degrees, is put back in silly clues

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the jumbled letters
silly suggests the letters of clues are jumbled into a nonsense order
put back tells us to write the word is in reverse order

explanation.surface: A scientist, honoured by university degrees, gets returned to a set of daft puzzle clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remembered by degrees' is part of the definition: the temperature scale keeps his name alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Celsius, the Swedish astronomer, is commemorated in the temperature scale measured in degrees named after him.

clue.text: Keep going in university after second bad mark

indicators.note: after puts university following the letter for second

parts.note: a stain is a blemish or mark

explanation.surface: A student carries on at university after getting a second poor grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain or continue it, keeping it alive over time.

clue.text: Flop Gilbert and Sullivan initially backed

indicators.note: backed means the picked letters are read from back to front
initially picks the opening letter of each of the three words Gilbert, and, Sullivan

explanation.surface: A comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan was a failure, though at first it had financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes G, A, S from Gilbert, and, Sullivan; 'backed' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To flop is to droop or hang down limply, which is what something that sags does.

clue.text: Irregular dieting is no problem for eater

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of dieting, is, no are not in their usual order

explanation.surface: Erratic dieting causes no trouble for someone who eats.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface claims eaters have no problem, but 'no' is anagram fodder and the problem is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia, or discomfort in digesting food, is a typical complaint of someone who has eaten.

clue.text: Promoter taking in politician and his leader is liar

indicators.note: taking in means the promoter word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a seller promotes and markets goods
a Tory is a British Conservative
his refers back to the politician, so his leader is the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A publicist enlisting a politician, along with that politician's party leader, is a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his leader' is the first letter of TORY, not of 'his'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of tales, in childish usage, is one who fibs.

clue.text: Claim as part of historical legend

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something asserted as being in an old tale from history.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is a claim.

clue.text: Left, in protest, is hard to break up

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A left-wing demonstrator finds a protest hard to dissolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish a building is to pull it down and smash it to pieces.

clue.text: With lawyers, first of all, the answer is material

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word all

explanation.surface: Consulting lawyers, the solution above all is the material evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' looks like 'firstly', but it picks the first letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen cloth often used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Ambassador and I told a PM off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of I told a PM have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An envoy confesses to having scolded the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told off' reads as a scolding, but 'told' is fodder and 'off' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior envoy representing his country abroad, a kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Take the lead in bridge section, holding ace

indicators.note: holding means the bridge part contains the ace word

parts.note: a pier is a support pillar of a bridge
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: At the card table, lead off in a hand of bridge while holding an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' and 'ace' suggest cards, but a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge span.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to be first to develop something, going ahead of others.

clue.text: Persian king seizing power in divided island

indicators.note: seizing means the king's name grabs and holds the power letter within it

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian empire
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An ancient Persian monarch takes control of a split island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island has been split between Greek and Turkish Cypriot zones since 1974.

clue.text: Friendly relations chat over wine

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a rap is a talk or chat
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Conversation over a glass of wine builds amicable ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious understanding between people.

clue.text: Very large vessel carrying one person on watch?

indicators.note: carrying means the pieces hold the numeral within them

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A huge ship with one lookout aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a sentry; the question mark flags that it means watching a screen or event.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer is someone who looks at something, such as a television audience member.

clue.text: Evita Peron I backed, exchanging two letters — producing no effect

indicators.note: exchanging two letters says a pair of letters in the turned string swap places
backed means Evita Peron I is read from the end to the start

explanation.surface: Evita Perón got financial support, but swapping a couple of letters changed nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns EVITA PERON I into INOREPATIVE; 'exchanging two letters' swaps R and P so REP becomes PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inoperative is not working, so it has no effect or result.

clue.text: Vegetable or fruit cropped once or twice

indicators.note: cropped means the fruit's tail is cut off; once from a four-letter fruit, or twice from a five-letter one

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A green vegetable or a fruit that has been trimmed one or two times.
explanation.walkthrough: Either PEAR loses its last letter once, or PEACH loses its last letter twice; both leave the same pod vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The small round green seed grown in pods is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bunk, I said, used to be a little hot

indicators.note: said signals that the word I is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: the letter I sounds the same as the word for the organ of sight
was is the past tense of be
H is a small part, the first letter, of hot

explanation.surface: Someone claims a bed used to be slightly warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed, but it means nonsense here. H is the abbreviation for hot found on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is short for bunkum, meaning nonsense, and eyewash is likewise humbug or rubbish.

clue.text: Piece of circular curve

indicators.note: piece of says a short run of letters sits within the words circular curve

parts.note: the letters run from the end of circular into curve

explanation.surface: A section of a round bend.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a segment of a circle's circumference, a bowed line.

clue.text: Organised workers give approval to rule backing strike

indicators.note: backing means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: TU is a trade union, an organisation of workers
to OK something is to approve it
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A trade union endorses a regulation that supports industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for the strike, but it reverses TU, OK and LAW together.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout is a strike in which workers leave their workplace in protest.

clue.text: Theoretician who doesn't have to stand up for his opinions?

definitions.text: Theoretician who doesn't have to stand up for his opinions?

parts.words: Theoretician who doesn't have to stand up for his opinions?
parts.note: stand up means defend, but literally this critic stays seated in a comfy chair while judging

explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up for' usually means defend, but here it is literal: this critic gives views without getting out of a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic judges from comfort with no practical experience, offering theory only.
